title: Stable reduction over finite-height separably closed valuation fields
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed] field [def-weil-field] and $V\subset K$ a valuation ring: its fraction field is $K$ and for every $a\in K^\times$ at least one of $a,a^{-1}$ belongs to $V$. Assume $V$ has finite height, meaning that its prime ideals form a finite chain. Let $(X,D)$ be a multipointed curve over $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] whose generic curve is smooth and generic marking is etale. Then $(X,D)$ admits a stable $\eta$-modification over $T$ itself. A multipointed curve $(X,D)$ over a scheme $T$ means flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphisms $X\to T$, $D\to T$ of pure relative dimensions $1$, $0$ and a closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; $D$ may be empty and $X$ need not be separated or proper over $T$. It is semistable if every singular point of every geometric fibre has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field, $D\to T$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $D$ lies in the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For integral $T$ with generic point $\eta$, an $\eta$-modification of multipointed curves is a compatible pair $f_X:X'\to X$, $f_D:D'\to D$ of proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism], each an isomorphism over a schematically dense open and on its generic fibre. A semistable such modification is stable if in each geometric fibre there is no irreducible component isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1$ that is contracted by $f_X$ and meets the union of the marking and the singular points of $X'$ in at most two points. Geometric fibres are [def-weil-geometric-fibre]; dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; the local completion is at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $\Omega[[u,v]]$ denotes the two-variable formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Here an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense when $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective.

source.place: Proposition 4.5.1, p. 33; smooth-generic-fibre case of its proof, using Propositions 4.3.3, 4.3.1, 4.4.6 and Corollary 4.4.3. No Noetherian or discreteness assumption on V.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-valuation-horizontal-curve-models] to $(X,D)$. In particular $X$ is reduced with finitely many components, and any reduced modification of $X$ is again a finitely presented flat $T$-curve, with the marking extended by schematic closure. It is legitimate to work with the centred valuations of each generic component separately; no assertion that connectedness of $X$ forces connectedness of $X_\eta$ is needed. The empty curve case has the identity stable modification, so assume $X$ nonempty. Apply [lem-trf-valuation-strict-semistable-local-uniformization] to get finitely many integral strictly semistable quasi-modifications $Y_i\to X$ on which all these valuations have centres. All generic opens of $Y_i$ are smooth.

source.place: Proposition 4.5.1, first paragraph and invocation of Proposition 4.3.3, p. 33

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-birational-quasi-modification-common-cover] on this finite valuation cover. It gives a reduced proper modification $X_1\to X$ and an open cover $X_1=\bigcup W_i$, with modifications $W_i\to Y_i$ over $X$. Here $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated because it is finitely presented over the affine base. By [lem-trf-valuation-horizontal-curve-models], $(X_1,D_1)$, with $D_1$ the closure of $D_\eta$, is a multipointed $T$-curve and an $\eta$-modification of $(X,D)$. Its restriction $(W_i,E_i)$ is the horizontal marked model on $W_i$. The generic fibre of $W_i\to Y_i$ is an isomorphism, since it is a modification of a smooth curve, as included in the same horizontal-model node applied to $Y_i$ with empty marking.

source.place: Proposition 4.5.1, common modification C prime and its cover C_i prime, p. 33

proof.text: Fix $i$. Apply [lem-trf-valuation-strict-semistable-cofinality] to the modification $W_i\to Y_i$ of the strictly semistable $T$-curve $Y_i$. Obtain a strictly semistable $Z_i$ with an $\eta$-modification $Z_i\to W_i$. Since $Z_i$ is a $T$-curve with smooth generic fibre $Z_{i,\eta}\cong W_{i,\eta}$, the reducedness clause of [lem-trf-valuation-horizontal-curve-models] applied to $(Z_i,\emptyset)$ shows that $Z_i$ is reduced, so $Z_i\to W_i$ is a reduced modification. Give $Z_i$ the schematic closure $F_i$ of the generic marking of $W_i$. By [lem-trf-valuation-horizontal-curve-models], this is a multipointed curve and $(Z_i,F_i)\to(W_i,E_i)$ is an $\eta$-modification of pairs; importantly, one does not take the full inverse image of the marking. The generic marking is etale and the generic curve is smooth. Thus [lem-trf-valuation-marking-semistable-separation] gives a semistable $\eta$-modification $(\widetilde Z_i,\widetilde F_i)\to(Z_i,F_i)$. Composing the two proper maps, on both curves and markings, gives a semistable $\eta$-modification of $(W_i,E_i)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](a). For schematic density of the composite, intersect the two dense isomorphism opens where the composition is defined by isomorphisms. This intersection is dense on every component of the smooth generic fibre. On each flat affine chart its ring injects into its generic localization, a reduced ring, and then into sections on this generic dense open. Thus the intersection is schematically dense on source and target.

source.place: Proposition 4.5.1, applications of Proposition 4.3.1 and Lemma 4.3.2, p. 33

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-valuation-semistable-stable-contraction] to each semistable modification from Step 3, obtaining a stable $\eta$-modification $f_i:(S_i,H_i)\to(W_i,E_i)$. These are stable relative to $W_i$, not yet relative to $X$. Restrict to $W_{ij}=W_i\cap W_j$. The restrictions are still multipointed curves and proper $\eta$-modifications, using [lem-trf-valuation-horizontal-curve-models] for closures and generic identifications and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b) for properness. They are semistable because this is a condition on the local rings and the marking. Stability is preserved under this target restriction: a contracted component over a point of $W_{ij}$ is entirely contained in its inverse image, and its marking and singular intersection points are the same as before restriction. Thus an exceptional projective line here would already be exceptional for $f_i$.

source.place: Proposition 4.5.1, local stable modifications and restriction to the overlaps, p. 33

proof.text: The base $T$ is normal: if $z\in K\setminus V$ were integral over $V$, then $z^{-1}$ would be a nonunit of $V$; multiplying a monic integral equation for $z$ by $z^{-n}$ would give $1\in(z^{-1})$, a contradiction. Localizations of $V$ are valuation rings by the same divisibility test and are integrally closed by the same argument. The affine integral scheme $T$ is also quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Consequently [lem-trf-stable-modification-uniqueness-normal] applies to the two restricted stable modifications of $(W_{ij},D_1|_{W_{ij}})$: their generic curve is smooth, their generic marking is etale, and their generic identifications agree. It yields a unique isomorphism $\alpha_{ij}$ over this pair. Empty intersections use the unique empty isomorphism. On a triple overlap both $\alpha_{jk}\alpha_{ij}$ and $\alpha_{ik}$ are isomorphisms over the same target pair; uniqueness makes them equal. This supplies the cocycle, rather than assuming that chosen local models agree.

source.place: Proposition 4.5.1, uniqueness on intersections; Corollary 4.4.3 is the source local uniqueness argument, p. 33

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes] separately to the $S_i$ and to the $H_i$, with the inverse images of $W_{ij}$ as overlap opens and the cocycle of Step 5. This produces $(S,H)$ over $(X_1,D_1)$. Maps to the target and the marking immersions glue: their continuous maps and sheaf homomorphisms agree on intersections, and the marking ideals agree there. The result is a closed marking. Flatness, finite presentation and the pure fibre dimensions hold on these finite open covers; for finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness follow by gluing over the finite cover $W_i$ of the finitely presented $X_1$. Semistability is checked in the same local rings as before. Properness of both pair maps is local on the target: finite type and the closed diagonal are local there, and closed images after any base change are checked on the corresponding open cover. Hence the glued pair map is proper. Its generic fibre is the identity by the chosen identifications, and its local dense isomorphism opens give schematic density as in Step 3. Finally, every contracted projective-line component is contained in the inverse image of some $W_i$, so the same argument as Step 4 proves stability relative to $(X_1,D_1)$. We have constructed a semistable (indeed stable) $\eta$-modification of $(X_1,D_1)$.

source.place: Proposition 4.5.1, gluing the local stable models, p. 33

proof.text: Compose $(S,H)\to(X_1,D_1)\to(X,D)$. Both maps on the curve and marking are proper, so their composites are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](a). They are generic-fibre isomorphisms; intersect their dense isomorphism opens as in Step 3. The intersection is dense on each component of the generic curve (and is the whole generic marking); injection of flat affine rings into generic localizations and then into sections on these dense opens proves schematic density. Thus the composite is a semistable $\eta$-modification of $(X,D)$. It need not be stable relative to $X$, since the intermediate map may contract more components. Apply [lem-trf-valuation-semistable-stable-contraction] once more, now relative to $(X,D)$, to obtain the required stable $\eta$-modification over $T$ itself. No extension of the valuation field or alteration of $T$ was introduced.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q93-57b4f104b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all six new nodes, the cited statements (uniqueness-normal, glue-schemes, proper-fp-permanence and the definition nodes), the unit sk-i-curve-zero and the neighbouring Temkin and de Jong nodes in full. The item statement is unchanged and is not weakened, and the parent lem-trf-temkin-stable-modification step 2 uses it exactly as stated. The seven steps are correct. Step 1: local uniformization over the finitely many generic components. Step 2: one proper modification X_1 covered by the W_i. Step 3: strict cofinality, then marking separation. Step 4: local contraction, with stability kept on the overlaps. Step 5: the cocycle comes from uniqueness over normal T, and the integral-closedness of a valuation ring and its localizations is checked. Step 6: gluing. Step 7: compose and contract again relative to X, since stability relative to X_1 does not give it relative to X. I proved the two general new nodes myself: the common cover (Nagata compactification per component closure, a closure in the fibre product, and covering by separatedness) and the horizontal models (all generic points lie over eta, so the model is torsion-free and flat; flat finite type over a valuation ring gives finite presentation; finite birational onto a normal curve is an isomorphism; schematic closure of the marking). I tested the other four at height zero, with an empty curve, an already strict or stable model, and nonseparated marking closures; they are plausible inputs and none restates the item. There are no duplicates in the DAG (Riemann-Zariski refinement, spreading, flatification and proper-birational nodes all compared), no cycle, and uses equal proof_deps. Faults repaired in fixes/: (1) B3: 'separably closed' had no definition in the item or in five new nodes, so I cited def-kun-separably-closed and added it to stmt_deps; (2) B3: horizontal-models used 'modification' without defining it and left 'irreducible components' uncited, as did local-uniformization, so I added the inline definition and def-weil-irreducible-components; (3) step 3 of the item did not say why Z_i is reduced, so I added one sentence from the already-cited horizontal node. Limitation: the Temkin PDF is not in literature/ and I have no network, so I could not check the Temkin page and proposition places. The delivery marks this as agent-origin with a WANTED line, and I checked the mathematics independently.
